edges.description: Continued lipid accumulation, foam-cell death, and matrix remodeling mature the formed carotid plaque into a cap-and-core atheroma.
intermediate_mechanisms: Continued lipid accumulation and foam-cell death enlarge the necrotic core.
Smooth-muscle-cell switching and matrix remodeling build and reshape the fibrous cap.

edges.description: Progressive atherosclerotic plaque can culminate in non-acute internal carotid occlusion, but the cohort does not resolve whether rupture, thrombosis, or chronic occlusive remodeling supplies the intermediates.
Completed carotid occlusion can reduce downstream blood flow or generate embolic ischemia in cerebral and retinal territories.

Raised pressure and shear injure the endothelium, and the lipid retention, foam-cell accumulation, and inflammatory remodelling that follow are the steps this node already sets out. Those intermediates are known, which is why the link is indirect rather than direct.

Diabetes drives atherogenesis through hyperglycemic endothelial injury and dyslipidemia, reaching carotid plaque by the same intermediates this node describes. The cited case-control study is carotid specific, though the quoted sentence states the determinant relationship for atherosclerosis generally.

Modifiable lifestyle exposures feeding the same endothelial injury and lipid retention sequence as hypertension. Graded identically to the hypertension link in this entry because both rest on the same sentence of the same review.

nodes.description: Continued lipid accumulation, foam-cell death, and matrix remodeling produce an advanced carotid atheroma with a lipid-rich necrotic core enclosed by a fibrous cap. Neovascularization, intraplaque hemorrhage, cap thinning, and surface ulceration can destabilize the lesion. This optional mature-plaque stage is represented without assuming that it caused every chronic or non-acute occlusion in the cited cohorts.
nodes.id: Advanced carotid atheroma with necrotic core and fibrous cap

evidence.reference_title: Molecular Pathways of Vulnerable Carotid Plaques at Risk of Ischemic Stroke: A Narrative Review
evidence.snippet: In macroscopic evaluation, vulnerable plaques are characterized by one or more of the following features: microcalcification; neovascularization; lipid-rich necrotic cores (LRNCs); intraplaque hemorrhage (IPH); thin fibrous caps; plaque surface ulceration; huge dimensions, suggesting stenosis; and plaque rupture.

evidence.reference_title: The microenvironment of the atheroma expresses phenotypes of plaque instability.
evidence.snippet: the local arterial microenvironment of a stable atheroma promotes destabilizing conditions that result in the transition to an unstable atheroma.

nodes.description: Vascular smooth-muscle-cell phenotypic switching, proliferation, and extracellular-matrix secretion assemble a fibrofatty plaque with a fibrous cap in the carotid arterial wall. Progressive plaque growth creates the substrate for later stenosis and occlusion.

evidence.snippet: CS is seen undergoing almost the same pathogenesis of any atherosclerotic plaque formation, from endothelial damage of the artery lumen to the formation of a fibrous cap with a foam cell, lipid-filled core.

nodes.description: Endothelial injury in the carotid arterial wall permits infiltration and retention of apoB-containing lipoproteins in the intima. Local modification of retained LDL initiates the inflammatory plaque-forming branch that can progress toward atherosclerotic carotid occlusion.

evidence.reference_title: The Role of Lipids and Lipoproteins in Atherosclerosis.
evidence.snippet: infiltration and retention of apoB containing lipoproteins in the artery wall is a critical initiating event that sparks an inflammatory response and promotes the development of atherosclerosis.

nodes.description: Recruited carotid-intimal monocytes become macrophages, internalize modified apoB lipoproteins, and form lipid-laden foam cells. Macrophage inflammation amplifies LDL oxidation, endothelial activation, and additional monocyte recruitment in the plaque-forming branch.

evidence.reference_title: The Role of Lipids and Lipoproteins in Atherosclerosis.
evidence.snippet: Internalization of the apoB containing lipoproteins by macrophages promotes foam cell formation, which is the hallmark of the fatty streak phase of atherosclerosis.

evidence.reference_title: The Role of Lipids and Lipoproteins in Atherosclerosis.
evidence.snippet: Macrophage inflammation results in enhanced oxidative stress and cytokine/chemokine secretion, causing more LDL/remnant oxidation, endothelial cell activation, monocyte recruitment, and foam cell formation.

nodes.description: Atherosclerotic plaque growth and associated thrombotic or occlusive remodeling can produce non-acute or chronic long-segment occlusion of the internal carotid artery. Occlusion anatomy and plaque location influence recanalization feasibility and re-occlusion risk. The available cohort evidence does not distinguish acute rupture or erosion from chronic plaque growth and occlusive remodeling, so this node is not restricted to the rupture-driven atherogenesis consequence.

evidence.reference_title: Significance of atherosclerotic plaque location in recanalizing non-acute long-segment occlusion of the internal carotid artery.
evidence.snippet: To investigate the significance of atherosclerotic plaque location in hybrid surgery comprising both endovascular recanalization approaches and carotid endarterectomy for symptomatic atherosclerotic non-acute long-segment occlusion of the internal carotid artery (ICA), 162 patients were enrolled, including 120 (74.1%) patients in the proximal plaque group and 42 (25.9%) in the distal plaque group.
